findings.title: Long docked-header titles overflow instead of truncating on desktop
findings.description:
`.d-header .contents` is now `display: flex`, so its direct children become flex items. `header.hbs:94` renders `{{header-extra-info}}` as a direct child of `.contents`. However, `header-extra-info` is a plain `Ember.Component` with no `tagName` (`components/header-extra-info.js.es6:1`), so Ember wraps its template in a `div.ember-view`. That wrapper is the flex item, not `.extra-info-wrapper`.

The wrapper's automatic minimum width is its min-content width. `.topic-link` is `white-space: nowrap` (`desktop/topic-post.scss:532-538`), so that min-content equals the full title width. The `overflow: hidden` on `.extra-info-wrapper` (`desktop/topic-post.scss:518-519`) does not help, because it sits inside the flex item. The title therefore cannot shrink, the `text-overflow: ellipsis` never applies, and a long title can push `.panel` out of view. Under the old float layout, the `overflow: hidden` block formed a BFC beside the floats with a constrained width, so truncation worked.

I could not verify this in a browser. The conclusion comes from the CSS and templates. A fix would be `min-width: 0` on the wrapper, for example `.d-header .contents > .ember-view`. Check it with a long title at desktop width.

findings.title: Mobile small-action custom-message offset was not updated
findings.description: `.small-action .small-action-desc .custom-message` still sets `margin-left: -40px`. That value was tuned against the `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` that this diff removes from `.small-action-desc` (`common/base/topic-post.scss:280`). The description now starts right after the 45px avatar column with only `padding: 0 1.5%`. The -40px pull-back therefore moves the custom message about 40px left of the description box, into the avatar column. For small actions with `post.cooked`, that likely overlaps the avatar icon. I could not render this. The estimate comes from the CSS values. Adjust or remove the mobile margin as part of this change.

findings.title: `order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` has no effect
findings.description: `.extra-info-wrapper` sits inside the `div.ember-view` wrapper described above, so it is not a flex item and `@include order(2)` does nothing. The title sorts before `.panel` only because `.panel` has `order(3)` (`header.scss:39`) and the wrapper keeps the default order 0. Either remove the `order(2)` declaration or leave a comment that explains the ordering comes from `.panel`.

findings.title: `align-items` mixin has a dead declaration and formatting drift
findings.description: `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a property any browser implements, so the declaration is dead. The IE10 prefix is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already on line 120. Line 120 also has trailing whitespace, line 122 is missing the space after the colon used elsewhere in the file, and this mixin indents four spaces while `order()` indents two. Remove line 121 and tidy the formatting.

findings.title: No test or visual check covers these layout changes
findings.description: Nothing under `spec/` or `test/` references `.d-header`, `.small-action`, `.extra-info-wrapper`, or `.custom-message`. The only match for those terms is a JS fixture. The four layout changes (header flex, `.small-action` flex, `.bullet` badge display, and the mobile small-action padding) have no automated coverage and no visual check in the diff.

findings.title: Mixins are defined before every file that uses them
findings.description: `common/foundation/mixins` is imported at line 6, before `common/components/*` (line 8, which includes `badges.css.scss`) and `common/base/*` (line 12, which includes `header.scss`, `topic.scss`, and `topic-post.scss`). A repo-wide grep found no other definitions of `flexbox`, `inline-flex`, `align-items`, or `order`, so there are no collisions.

findings.title: Panel moves to the right edge correctly
findings.description: `.panel` is a direct child of `.contents` (`header.hbs:6`), so the `margin-left: auto` and `order(3)` declarations take effect. Removing `float: right` is safe, because a flex item ignores float.

findings.title: Small-action flex applies to the right elements
findings.description: The component sets `classNames: ['small-action']` (`small-action.js.es6:30`), so `.small-action` is its own root element. Its children, `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc`, are direct children (`small-action.hbs:1-2`). The flex and `align-items` declarations therefore land on the right element.
